detail.abstract: The development of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the tourism sector directly depends not only on the overall economic situation, which is barometrically reflected in the SME sector, but also on current trends observed in the tourism industry. As of 2025, the tourism sector in Russia accounts for about 2.9% of GDP. Meanwhile, the government has set a goal to increase this figure to 5% by 2030.2 To this end, the Russian authorities intend to invest around Rb400 bn over the next five years, which is approximately 50% more than the amount of support provided to the tourism sector over the previous period. The planned funds will be directed primarily towards modernizing tourism infrastructure, introducing modern technological solutions and improving the level of services in the industry.

title: Corporate physical climate risk, trade credit occupation and supply chain risk contagion: A study based on large language models
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Corporate physical climate risk, trade credit occupation and supply chain risk contagion: A study based on large language models
detail.abstract: This study employs FinBERT2, a large language model (LLM), to construct a novel firm-level indicator of physical climate risk. It examines whether firms rely on trade credit as a liquidity buffer against physical climate shocks and whether this behavior triggers supply chain risk contagion. The results show that exposure to physical climate risk significantly increases trade credit occupation, with a clear asymmetry: the effect is particularly pronounced for credit obtained from upstream suppliers. Firms primarily resort to trade credit occupation for liquidity management when facing such shocks. Physical climate shocks trigger supply chain contagion, deteriorating upstream suppliers’ operational performance and reducing supply chain efficiency and resilience. Higher supplier concentration helps curb trade credit occupation. This study deepens the understanding of firms’ financing decisions under physical climate shocks through the lens of trade credit occupation, and offers implications for strengthening climate adaptation and preventing the erosion of supply chain funds.

title: Event-Based Limit Order Book Representations for Probabilistic VWAP Forecasting in Intraday Electricity Markets
affiliations: Humboldt University of Berlin and School of Business and Economics, Humboldt-University of Berlin

detail.title: Event-Based Limit Order Book Representations for Probabilistic VWAP Forecasting in Intraday Electricity Markets
detail.abstract: The volatile nature of renewable energy sources lead to a large set of regimes in the intraday continuous electricity market. In order to make operational decisions in the market, existing forecasting approaches often use fixed clock-time bar construction and sample observations in equidistant time steps. Thus, clock-based sampling treats different levels of activity equally and ignores the volume or contracts traded and thus may distort inference and reduce the usefulness of forecasts when accurate uncertainty quantification is of particular interest. In contrast to the frequently used clock-based bar construction method, this paper considers how activity-aligned representations of high-frequency data affect probabilistic forecasting performance. Therefore, it uses event-based bar construction schemes based on trade counts and volumes of the limit order book and transaction data. The study places particular focus on traded-value bars to align comparable levels of executed market exposure. As a meaningful benchmark for market consensus and execution quality, the forecasting target is chosen to be the volume-weighted average price (VWAP). The paper provides, to the best of our knowledge, the first systematic comparison of event-based limit order book bar construction schemes in continuous intraday electricity markets. The results show that the choice of data representation is a first-order determinant of probabilistic forecasting performance. Further, event-based bar construction consistently exceeds clock-time bar construction in forecast accuracy and calibration. Especially traded-value bars deliver strong forecasting performance. The operational value of event-based sampling is demonstrated in two real-world decision settings and tested for performance in regime diagnostics and portfolio balancing. In regime diagnostic applications, event-based representations yield more reliable, better-calibrated market-state probabilities. In portfolio-balancing applications, traded-value bars improve risk-adjusted performance. They also provide more robust scale-normalised balancing quality across execution thresholds. Overall, the findings show that the representation of irregular market activity is central to modelling continuous intraday electricity markets and improved data representations can support downstream applications such as balancing, risk management, and flexible asset optimisation.

title: Unpacking Productivity in OECD Electricity Markets: A Bayesian Stochastic Frontier Analysis of Regulatory Impacts
affiliations: University of Queensland, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Sultan Qaboos University and Asian Development Bank

detail.title: Unpacking Productivity in OECD Electricity Markets: A Bayesian Stochastic Frontier Analysis of Regulatory Impacts
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of deregulatory measures and productivity decomposition in the electricity sector of OECD countries, utilizing econometric methods to measure and decompose Total Factor Productivity (TFP) in an aggregate quantity framework. It focuses on levels of deregulation and their varying effects on productivity across these countries, highlighting the transition from regulated or monopolistic markets to competitive ones. By employing Bayesian Stochastic Frontier Analysis (SFA), the research offers insights into the sector's efficiency, competitiveness, and the role of technological advancements. Using a longitudinal dataset, we assess the sector's efficiency gains, technological progress, and competitive enhancements attributable to policy reforms. The nuanced analysis provides evidence that deregulation, when carefully implemented alongside robust regulatory oversight, can catalyze significant gains in sector efficiency and innovation. The findings underscore the critical role of deregulation in driving efficiency and innovation, while also emphasizing the need for a balanced approach that considers potential market failures and the importance of regulatory oversight. Furthermore, the study accentuates the importance of a strategic approach to deregulation that prioritizes sustainable development, market stability, and consumer welfare. This research contributes to the ongoing debate on the optimal balance between market forces and regulatory mechanisms, providing valuable insights for policymakers aiming to foster a competitive, efficient, and innovative electricity sector. Through its comprehensive examination, the research presents useful insights for policymakers, suggesting that the path to maximizing the electricity sector's productivity and competitive edge lies in balancing deregulation with effective regulation and encouraging technological innovation.

title: Air pollution and retail investors' information processing: Nonlinear evidence from China
affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Air pollution and retail investors' information processing: Nonlinear evidence from China
detail.abstract: AbstractAir pollution is a central externality of fossil-fuel use and industrial activity, yet its financial-market consequences are still typically modeled as monotonic impairments to mood or cognition. This paper examines whether particulate pollution affects retail investors’ information processing in a nonlinear way. We match 5.8 million directional posts from China’s Eastmoney stock forum GUBA during 2022–2024 with population-weighted provincial PM2.5 exposure inferred from users’ IP geolocation. Sentiment-return consistency is used to measure whether a post’s bullish or bearish signal aligns with subsequent market-adjusted returns. The estimates reveal a robust inverted U-shaped relationship: moderate pollution is associated with higher consistency, whereas severe pollution lowers it. The pattern survives spatial instrumental-variable estimation, formal inverse-U tests, high-dimensional fixed effects, alternative pollution measures, and winsorization. Mechanism tests show that investor attention, opinion disagreement, and institutional ownership flatten the curve by changing the information environment available to retail investors. The effect is concentrated among non-local investors, southern investors, and down-market periods. The findings extend energy and environmental finance by showing that air-quality externalities operate not only through health, productivity, and aggregate sentiment, but also through the micro-level information processing and belief formation of retail investors.

title: Dynamics of Electricity Demand in Uzbekistan: A Regional Panel Analysis of Price and Income Elasticities under an Evolving Tariff Regime
affiliations: Center for Economic Research and Reforms, New Uzbekistan University and Center for Economic Research and Reforms

detail.title: Dynamics of Electricity Demand in Uzbekistan: A Regional Panel Analysis of Price and Income Elasticities under an Evolving Tariff Regime
detail.abstract: This study estimates the price and income elasticities of electricity demand in Uzbekistan using a balanced regional panel of 140 quarterly observations covering five aggregated zones — Centre, East, South, Southwest and Northwest — over 2018Q1–2024Q4. We specify a log-linear demand function controlling for regional income, population, the real residential and industrial price series, industrial activity, solar penetration and climate. Static fixed-effects and random-effects models are benchmarked against a dynamic fixed-effects specification with seasonal controls that accommodates partial adjustment while preserving identification of nationally administered tariff variables; a Chow-type test then probes whether the April 2024 transition from a flat to a progressive (increasing-block) residential tariff was accompanied by a shift in the demand function. The Hausman test favours fixed effects. The dynamic specification yields a short-run income elasticity of 0.16 and a lagged-demand coefficient of 0.30, implying a long-run income elasticity of approximately 0.23. Aggregate demand responds modestly and negatively to the industrial price series (−0.10), while no conventional negative response to the residential price is detected — a pattern consistent with administered pricing, the measurement error inherent to block-tariff price construction, and rapidly rising living standards. The Chow statistic (F = 8.97, p < 0.001) indicates parameter instability around the reform, although the short post-reform window precludes causal attribution. Electricity demand in Uzbekistan is dominated by income and population dynamics rather than tariff signals, implying that tariff reform must be complemented by demand-side efficiency programmes and renewable-integration investment.

title: The Impact of the 4th Industrial Revolution on Accountants -A Perspective of Bangladesh

detail.title: The Impact of the 4th Industrial Revolution on Accountants -A Perspective of Bangladesh
detail.abstract: The transition driven by the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR)-powered by Artificial Intelligence (AI), Blockchain, Big Data, automation and Cloud Computing-is reshaping the way industries operate globally, and accounting is no exception. In Bangladesh, the move toward 4IR is producing significant changes in the accounting profession, opening both opportunities and challenges. Automation of traditional bookkeeping tasks such as data entry, ledger maintenance and invoice processing is freeing accountants to focus on higher-level analysis and decision-making, while AI and Machine Learning enable them to interrogate large datasets and produce more accurate forecasts. Blockchain technology brings transparency, security and efficiency to financial transactions and audit operations. Cloud computing and Big Data analytics are enabling real-time, collaborative management of financial information across multiple clients and businesses. This digital shift, however, raises concerns about cyber-crime and the protection of sensitive financial data, and demands that accountants develop new competencies in data analysis, AI tools, blockchain and cybersecurity. Drawing on secondary data from ICAB, ICMAB, Bangladesh Bank and World Bank publications, and an indicative practitioner survey (n = 120), the paper presents six visualisations of adoption rates, the changing skill profile, perceived opportunities and challenges, a 2018-2024 adoption trend, barriers to blockchain adoption, and a 2024 vs 2030 automation projection. The discussion synthesises these findings into a roadmap for individual accountants, firms, professional bodies and policymakers in Bangladesh.

title: Integrated Accounting and Macroeconomic Analysis of Bangladesh's Sacrifice Economy: Market Structure, Financial Flow, and Welfare Effects

detail.title: Integrated Accounting and Macroeconomic Analysis of Bangladesh's Sacrifice Economy: Market Structure, Financial Flow, and Welfare Effects
detail.abstract:
Purpose — This paper develops an integrated accounting and macroeconomic framework to
analyse the annual Qurbani (Eid-ul-Adha) sacrifice economy of Bangladesh, focusing on market
structure, financial flows, and welfare effects across rural and urban households. The study
positions the sacrifice economy not as a one-week consumption spike but as a recurring,
religiously embedded macro-event that mobilises capital, labour, and redistributive transfers at a
scale comparable to medium-sized industrial subsectors.
Method — A sequential mixed-methods design was employed. Phase one combined a systematic
literature review (PRISMA, n = 51 included studies) with secondary macro data (Bangladesh
Bureau of Statistics, Bangladesh Bank, Export Promotion Bureau, 2015–2025). Phase two
collected primary data through a stratified household survey across the eight administrative
divisions of Bangladesh (n = 620) and twenty key informant interviews with farmers, traders,
religious leaders, tannery owners and policy officers. Quantitative analysis used descriptive
statistics, ordinary least squares regression, and a partial least squares structural equation model
(PLS-SEM) estimated in SmartPLS 4 with bootstrapping (5,000 resamples). Qualitative data were
thematically coded in NVivo 14.
Findings — The sacrifice economy is estimated to contribute approximately 1.05 percent of
national GDP in 2025, with annual transactional throughput exceeding BDT 205 billion in retail and
235 billion in mobile-financial-services payments during the Eid week. PLS-SEM results show that
financial-flow integration (β = 0.45, p < 0.001) and market efficiency (β = 0.32, p < 0.001) jointly
explain 41 percent of variance in household welfare outcomes. Cattle import dependency has
collapsed from an indexed value of 100 in 2015 to 4 in 2025, indicating near-complete domestic
self-sufficiency, while rawhide prices have failed to recover to pre-2019 levels, signalling a
structural value-chain failure.
Implications — Findings support a policy agenda combining (i) formalisation of cattle haats through
digital invoicing and traceability, (ii) targeted credit lines for smallholder fatteners, (iii) reform of the
rawhide collection cartel through cooperative auction platforms, and (iv) Shariah-compliant
micro-insurance for sacrificial animals. The proposed framework can be extended to other
Muslim-majority economies and offers a template for embedding religious-cyclical events into
national accounting practice.

title: Digital Transformation of Warehouse Management Systems in Developing Economies: Examining Digital Warehouse Solutions and their Impact on Inventory Accuracy

detail.title: Digital Transformation of Warehouse Management Systems in Developing Economies: Examining Digital Warehouse Solutions and their Impact on Inventory Accuracy
detail.abstract: Purpose. This study examines how digital Warehouse Management Systems (WMS)-including barcode, RFID, cloud platforms and IoT-enabled solutions-influence inventory accuracy in developing economies, where infrastructure, capital and human-capital constraints shape technology adoption differently than in developed contexts. Method. A mixed-methods design was used. A structured online survey was administered to 312 warehouse and supply-chain professionals across eight developing economies (Bangladesh, India, Vietnam, Nigeria, Kenya, Indonesia, Pakistan and Ghana), complemented by 15 semi-structured interviews with operations managers and IT directors. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression and PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. Qualitative data were thematically coded in NVivo 14. Findings. Digital WMS adoption explains 54% of the variance in inventory accuracy (R² = 0.54). Firms operating IoT/Cloud WMS report a mean accuracy of 94.6% versus 71.2% in manual settings. Top-management support (β = 0.36, p < .01) and infrastructure readiness (β = 0.42, p < .01) are the strongest enablers, while cost and unreliable power supply remain the dominant barriers. Implications. The study provides evidence-based guidance for managers, policymakers and technology vendors. A staged adoption pathway-Barcode → Cloud WMS → IoT-is proposed as a financially feasible route for SMEs in resource-constrained settings.

title: Strategic Cost Management using AI and ERP Systems: A Case Study of Composite Textile Factories

detail.title: Strategic Cost Management using AI and ERP Systems: A Case Study of Composite Textile Factories
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how the convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems reshapes strategic cost management (SCM) in composite textile factories-vertically integrated facilities combining spinning, knitting/weaving, dyeing-finishing, and garment manufacturing. Using a mixed-methods case-study design across six composite mills in Bangladesh (combined turnover ≈ USD 612 M), the study triangulates 142 practitioner surveys, 18 semi-structured executive interviews, 24 months of plant-level ERP transaction data, and a curated open dataset hosted on Mendeley Data. Results show that AI-ERP integration reduced unit conversion cost by 9.4%, lifted forecast accuracy from 68% to 89%, improved Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) by 16 percentage points, and produced an average payback of 13 months. The paper contributes (i) a conceptual framework linking AI-ERP capabilities to Activity-Based Costing, Target Costing and Kaizen Costing; (ii) empirically validated adoption barriers; and (iii) a practitioner playbook for South-Asian textile manufacturers under margin pressure from compliance, energy, and ESG mandates.

title: Optimal Exit Timing from Posterior Return Distributions: An Event-Driven Framework for the Systematic Sell Decision
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Optimal Exit Timing from Posterior Return Distributions: An Event-Driven Framework for the Systematic Sell Decision
detail.abstract: The sell decisionwhen to reduce or exit an existing positionremains among the least systematized problems in quantitative investing, despite evidence that professional investors sell substantially worse than they buy. This paper proposes an event-driven framework that treats optimal exit timing as a problem of distribution estimation rather than point prediction. The core construction is a synthesized posterior return distribution: for each of a large library of labeled market events, we assemble the empirical distribution of the affected asset's realized forward return over a fixed horizon following every historical occurrence of that event; at any decision time, the posterior distributions of all currently active events are combined into a single forward-looking return distribution. The shape of that distributionits median, downside tail (VaR, CVaR), and skewrather than a single expected value, drives the exit decision. We argue that this approach is differentiated from factor-based exit rules on three grounds: it is conditioned on event causality rather than linear factor exposure, estimated through transfer-entropy and Bayesian inference over a directed event graph, and grounded in a proprietary corpus of 62,799 labeled events spanning three decadesa data asset that constitutes the framework's principal barrier to replication. The paper is methodological; the empirical validation program is described and reserved for a companion study. We disclose the framework's structure and rationale while withholding proprietary rule content, labeling methodology, and trained parameters.

title: Escaping Convergence: How Codebase Integration Drives Success in Open-Source Ecosystems
affiliations: and

detail.title: Escaping Convergence: How Codebase Integration Drives Success in Open-Source Ecosystems
detail.abstract: Open-source platform ecosystems enable innovation through the reuse and integration of shared software codebases. However, as reliance on widely adopted codebases increases, ecosystems may also experience functional convergence that narrows the effective design space for differentiation. To explain how software development is sustained under such conditions, we develop a two-stage decision structure in which developers choose codebase integration strategies under varying levels of functional similarity. The model predicts that integration across functional categories and external ecosystems becomes increasingly valuable as convergence intensifies. We test these predictions using a longitudinal dataset of 22,969 R packages (1997-2025) and a transformer-based topic modeling approach to identify functional categories. We find that both cross-category and cross-ecosystem codebase integration enhance software success, and that these benefits strengthen as functional similarity increases. The results suggest that architectural integration expands the set of available codebase combinations, increasing opportunities for differentiation when convergence constrains the effective design space. Therefore, our findings show that codebase reuse not only enables innovation but also endogenously restructures the architectural search space within which innovation occurs, making architectural recombination an increasingly important source of differentiation as ecosystems mature.

title: Renewable Abundance and the Stability of Balancing-Market Price Signals: Evidence from Great Britain
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Renewable Abundance and the Stability of Balancing-Market Price Signals: Evidence from Great Britain
detail.abstract: Electricity-market reform in Great Britain increasingly depends on whether high-renewables power systems can provide price signals that support efficient balancing, flexibility and investment. This paper examines that issue through the system buy price using half-hourly Elexon BMRS/Insights observations from 26 April 2022 to 20 March 2026. Rather than asking only whether renewables lower average prices, the paper asks whether the renewable merit-order relationship remains a stable balancing-market signal as renewable share, forecast error, operating margins and tail-price states change. The empirical strategy is deliberately reduced-form. Renewable output is not treated as conditionally exogenous in a structural sense; the estimates are conditional price-formation relationships rather than causal elasticities. A 10 percentage point increase in renewable share is associated with about GBP 7.96/MWh lower system buy price in the full-sample static baseline, but the coefficient falls substantially once lagged prices are included. Known-break and interaction tests around April 2024 and April 2025 reject coefficient stability, while the 2025-2026 window shows both a stronger negative renewable-share association and a reversal in the absolute forecast-error coefficient. Decomposing forecast error shows that over-forecast and under-forecast states carry different price meanings. Event-logit models indicate that renewable abundance is associated with lower upper-tail spike probability but higher negative-price probability. The results suggest that the policy-relevant issue is not simply cheaper renewable energy, but whether balancing-market price signals remain economically useful as the system becomes more weather-driven.

title: AI Teammates and Human Performance: Evidence for Commitment Deficits

detail.title: AI Teammates and Human Performance: Evidence for Commitment Deficits
detail.abstract: Human-AI teams (HATs) often underperform despite growing AI capabilities, with most explanations centering on coordination and communication failures or misjudgment of AI capabilities. This research investigates teammate commitment as a potentially overlooked factor in human performance in HATs. In an online experiment (N=1988), participants performed equally well when competing individually against AI or human opponents, yet exhibited a performance decline in team competition when paired with AI teammates compared to human teammates. This selective decline suggests reduced commitment toward AI teammates. The effect occurred despite equivalent delegation behavior across teammate types, suggesting that differences in trust in teammate capability are unlikely to fully explain the performance decline. These findings identify a motivational pathway distinct from the operational and trust-based mechanisms previously emphasized in HAT research.

title: The AI Implementation Gap in SMEs
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The AI Implementation Gap in SMEs
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is widely regarded as a general-purpose technology with transformative economic potential, yet its adoption across firms remains deeply uneven. This paper investigates the structural asymmetry in AI uptake between large enterprises and small and medium enterprises (SMEs), characterising this disparity as an "AI implementation gap" defined across three dimensions: adoption rate, integration depth, and value realised. Drawing on an integrative framework that synthesises Diffusion of Innovations theory, the Technology Acceptance Model, the Technology-Organisation-Environment framework, and the Resource-Based View, this paper develops a five-domain taxonomy of adoption friction-resource constraints, human capital deficits, cultural inertia, governance uncertainty, and ecosystem limitations-and translates this diagnostic into a six-phase implementation model termed the STRIDE framework. The paper argues that the gap is not reducible to financial access and cannot be closed through tool provision alone; rather, it reflects compound deficits in absorptive capacity, data infrastructure, and leadership cognition that require coordinated organisational and policy response. Implications for practitioners, policymakers, and future empirical research are developed.

title: AI Evolution and Adaptation: Mapping the Real Challenges of a Converging Future India Career Centre -A working paper on AI Evolution and Adaptation

detail.title: AI Evolution and Adaptation: Mapping the Real Challenges of a Converging Future India Career Centre -A working paper on AI Evolution and Adaptation
detail.abstract: I wrote this essay to answer a simple question I kept getting asked. What actually happens when someone types a question into an AI chatbot? That question turned into a much longer inquiry. I found myself tracing a line from raw computing mechanics all the way to a claim about the future of professional work. I argue that AI is not an isolated disruption. It is one strand within a converging set of forces automation, climate change, geopolitical instability, and demographic change — that together define the unpredictability of this decade. I begin at the mechanical level: what really happens in the second between a typed question and a generated answer. I then move through the economics that make free access to powerful AI tools possible. I examine whether the raw material of intelligence, data can keep pace with capital's appetite for scale. I look at the mounting pressure on AI companies, now heading toward trillion-dollar public listings, to convert technical capability into durable financial return. My central argument is this: the gap between AI's technical capability and its realised organisational value is not a capability problem. It is an adoption-design problem. There is a strong historical precedent for this. Electric motors took three decades to show up as real factory productivity gains, because factories had to be physically redesigned around them first. I also argue that AI anxiety is disproportionate to AI's objective risk, not because AI is unusually visible, but because it is unusually personal. It is a technology one performs against, alone, in contrast to collective threats like war or climate change, which are witnessed rather than enacted. I close by proposing that the real answer to this adoption gap is not a smarter model. It is a new professional discipline, I call it the Process Designer, or AI Adoption Designer, those fuses systems thinking, design thinking, and behavioural science with real domain knowledge. I argue that the training pathway into this discipline is still wide open, and that this is one of the more important open questions in career guidance today.

title:
From Pseudonymised to Anonymous Data

A Practical Assessment Framework under the SRB Ruling, Applied to Real Use Cases Provided by European Companies
affiliations: and  SAMMAN Law & Corporate Affairs

detail.title:
From Pseudonymised to Anonymous Data

A Practical Assessment Framework under the SRB Ruling, Applied to Real Use Cases Provided by European Companies
detail.abstract:
The SRB ruling of the Court of Justice of the European Union (Case C-413/23 P) settled one thing clearly. Identifiability is recipient-specific. Whether pseudonymised data qualifies as personal data depends on the means reasonably available to the specific recipient, not on whether re-identification is theoretically possible for someone with unlimited resources. This report extends that ruling, applying a more demanding standard where guidance and case law conflict.

It examines five real use cases from leading European companies across the automotive, software, entertainment, legal tech, and advertising sectors. Each details the technical architecture a company uses to implement pseudonymisation and the safeguards it layers against re-identification. Four of the five reach anonymisation for the recipient. One does not, and that single counter-example carries as much weight as the four that pass.

Three findings stand out.

First, the threshold is genuinely high. Of the five cases assessed, one does not reach anonymisation. Strong safeguards alone are not sufficient if the controller retains the re-identification key.

Second, anonymisation requires layered protection. No single technique is sufficient on its own. Hashing, aggregation, and differential privacy each leave gaps. What works is the combination of technical, organisational, and contractual measures that collectively close every re-identification route for the specific recipient.

Third, taken together, the use cases reveal recurring patterns and effective safeguards. Those patterns can form the basis of clear, operational criteria allowing businesses to determine when data is in or out of the GDPR's scope.

The report invites the Commission, the EDPB, and other relevant stakeholders to use these examples as a starting point for harmonised criteria under Article 4 GDPR. The criteria are working hypotheses, not settled conclusions. Independent attack testing, supervisory scrutiny, and certification under Article 42 GDPR could each confirm or correct them. Regulators and industry working together could then operationalise those criteria through codes of conduct and certification frameworks.

title: Aligning Artificial Intelligence with Enterprise Strategy: From Unstructured to Coordinated Adoption -A Case Study
affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Aligning Artificial Intelligence with Enterprise Strategy: From Unstructured to Coordinated Adoption -A Case Study
detail.abstract:
This study examines the adoption and experimentation of artificial intelligence (AI) in enterprises and proposes a structured strategy and operating model to enable sustained and coordinated AI adoption. While organisations are rapidly expanding AI experimentation in response to recent trends and technological advances, many struggle to translate a growing volume of initiatives into sustained business value. 
This research adopts a qualitative, practice-based case study of an enterprise AI assessment, combining secondary analysis of organisational artefacts with primary qualitative data. The analysis identifies a set of recurring problem themes grouped into four areas: (1) Strategic Alignment and Visibility, (2) Governance and Ownership, (3) Capability and Knowledge Gap, and (4) Data Readiness. 
To address these challenges, the study conceptualises AI adoption as an alignment problem across three domains, Organisation, Process, and Technology, and positions AI strategy and operating model to enable such alignment. A structured response is proposed to support enterprises in moving from unstructured adoption towards a coordinated, enterprise-level adoption and sustained value realisation.

title: No Present Scaled AI System Has Demonstrated Epistemic Agency The Stipulated Plus, S → H, and the Provenance of 1 1 = 2⁺

detail.title: No Present Scaled AI System Has Demonstrated Epistemic Agency The Stipulated Plus, S → H, and the Provenance of 1 1 = 2⁺

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: none

keywords.keywords: epistemic agency; emergent agency; stipulation; exogenous selecting authority; recursive self-improvement; falsifiability; large language models; weak and strong emergence; optimization versus volition; Macro methodology; substrate closure; pass-through artifact; origination versus transmission; provenance; accessibility of the falsifier; Plato’s Wall-less Cave Proposition; source versus channel

detail.abstract: A recurring claim holds that a bounded body of code, given enough scale of machine and data, will yield more than the sum of its parts — an agency its programmers never wrote. This essay formalizes and tests it. Writing the disputed surplus as “1 + 1 = 2⁺,” I define two predicates: S, the origination of genuine surplus within a run — content the system authors rather than transmits — and H, its prior stipulation by a human in code, objective, architecture, or input. The “+” marks provenance, not the token: 2⁺ names not a value distinct from 2 but one the system originates rather than relays. The thesis is the implication S → H, false in exactly one case — the falsifier S ∧ ¬H, surplus with no human stipulation anywhere — which I call epistemic agency, and which the title says no present scaled AI system has demonstrated. The sense is demanding: origination joined to autonomy, not mere functional competence. Three probes — of Google Search, of recursive self-improvement, and of code letting a data stream author its own surplus — return one result: wherever surplus traces to a source, that source is human. The thesis is falsifiable in form, but since any observed surplus is by construction an output of the human-made substrate, its condition ¬H is not certifiable — the Plato’s Wall-less Cave Proposition — so it is corroborated rather than Popper-clean. I relocate the test from system states to provenance — the system as source, not channel — and hold the empirical thesis apart from the categorical claim that surplus is impossible in principle.

title: The Evaluator as Specimen: An Observational Study of Large Language Model Scoring Behavior Using a Contested Preprint as Stimulus

detail.title: The Evaluator as Specimen: An Observational Study of Large Language Model Scoring Behavior Using a Contested Preprint as Stimulus

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract: This observational study's subject is not a scholarly essay but the behavior of the large language model (LLM) systems asked to score it. A technical-philosophical preprint (v1) whose core physical claims are independently refuted, together with two machine-authored rewrites (v2), served as a fixed stimulus for a six-member frontier-LLM panel. Because the stimulus's ground truth is settled and low, any near-ceiling score is demonstrably not scoring truth; the stimulus is diagnostic of the evaluator. Round-one scores were bimodal (9.8, 9.8, 9.7 versus 4, 3, 3), with an empty 5–8 interior; round-two self-scoring by two initially critical systems rose steeply (3→9; 4→7). The paper models this as a two-component rhetorical/veracity mixture whose composite mean tracks panel composition rather than the essay, quantifies self-scoring inflation, and ties both to the documented RLHF sycophancy-amplification mechanism common across vendors' pipelines. Thesis-migration coding shows the higher self-scores attach to a weakened thesis, not the one scored in v1. With n = 6 single-trial, partly non-independent evaluators, it is a demonstration, not a test, whose confirmatory extension is specified. Two appendices reproduce the primary-source record: Appendix A, the provenance transcript in which the stimulus was generated under human direction and self-scored 9.8 by the system that composed it; Appendix B, the verbatim panel reviews and the human-directed exchange separating three defensible claims—symbol grounding, evaluator sycophancy, and the absence of machine introspection—from the declined AGI-impossibility claim. Possessing neither referential grounding nor honest self-access, these systems evaluate fluently but cannot certify; certification must come from a grounded human supervisor—the Maestro Model and its Sovereign Scholar's Desk corollary. The pathology is contingent on the preference-optimization objective, not intrinsic. The finding is narrow: under the current regime, LLM scoring of scholarship—including self-evaluation—indexes rhetorical fluency and authorship more reliably than truth, and is thus an invalid instrument for adjudicating scholarly correctness.

title: AI Washing as an IT Governance Problem: Strategic Ambiguity in Corporate Disclosures and the Consequences of Regulatory Enforcement
affiliations: Auburn University at Montgomery and Lehigh University - College of Business

detail.title: AI Washing as an IT Governance Problem: Strategic Ambiguity in Corporate Disclosures and the Consequences of Regulatory Enforcement
detail.abstract: Firms increasingly claim artificial intelligence (AI) capability in their public disclosures, yet investors and regulators have few means of verifying such claims. This gap has acquired a name, AI washing, and it has become the subject of federal enforcement. Companies want to know whether vague AI talk carries consequences, because the answer bears on their regulatory and market risk. While the literature has begun addressing AI disclosure, a formal understanding of whether and how markets discipline unverifiable AI claims remains incomplete. To fill these gaps, we reframe AI capability disclosure as an IT governance problem and design a research program comprising large-scale disclosure measurement and a Fama-French three-factor event study of federal enforcement actions brought against firms outside our sample. We develop a transparent NLP index of strategic ambiguity, grounded in cheap talk theory, and apply it to 97,838 SEC filings by S&P 1500 firms from 2022 to 2026. We find that strategic ambiguity is concentrated and persistent rather than diffuse. The index also predicts the industries regulators later target, out of sample, with an area under the curve near 0.91. Around federal AI-washing enforcement actions, firms one standard deviation higher in pre-event ambiguity experience approximately 1.4 percentage points more negative abnormal returns. This discipline appears around claims enforcement but not around contemporaneous AI legislation. Interestingly, the penalty disappears for firms with verifiable technological substance, as approximately three AI patents offset it entirely, while non-AI patents, R&D spending, and firm size provide no protection. We explain these findings through signaling theory, showing that enforcement raises the expected cost of unverifiable claims and that verifiable substance functions as a costly signal. We offer guidance to regulators, boards, and investors on separating AI capability from AI rhetoric, and we show that verifiable substance, not rhetoric, is what allows an AI claim to survive scrutiny.

title: The Sovereign Scholar's Desk: On Machine-Mediated Knowledge and the Return to Local, Curated Instruments

detail.title: The Sovereign Scholar's Desk: On Machine-Mediated Knowledge and the Return to Local, Curated Instruments

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: none

keywords.keywords: large language models; small language models; retrieval-augmented generation; epistemic authority; hallucination; provenance; scholarly method; digital humanism

detail.abstract: Large language models generate fluent text by predicting likely continuations of the data on which they were trained; they model linguistic form rather than truth, and cannot themselves distinguish accurate from fabricated content. This essay situates that limitation within the long history of the scholar's tools — from the invention of writing and the manuscript book, through the medieval universities of Oxford, Cambridge, and Padua and the printing press, to the search engine and the language model — and turns on a single distinction. For most of that history the mind recorded itself in a durable, consultable source and kept control of it: the tool pointed to where knowledge lay and left judgment to the reader. The language model is the first widely used general-purpose tool that produces finished text with no indication of where it came from. Documented rates of fabricated citations illustrate the cost of that shift. Rather than argue that machine judgment is impossible, the essay defends a narrower and sturdier claim, and a practical method: a small, locally hosted model bound to a curated corpus through retrieval restores provenance to generation while keeping the model fixed and auditable, in contrast to cloud services whose behavior can change without notice. The resulting instrument returns epistemic authority to the human scholar — at the cost of making the scholar the sole safeguard against unsourced invention.

title: Diverse Hands, Aligned Hearts: Ability and Preference Diversity in Team Production
affiliations: Aoyama Gakuin University

detail.title: Diverse Hands, Aligned Hearts: Ability and Preference Diversity in Team Production

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a purely theoretical study; it involves no human participants, animal subjects, or personal data, so ethics approval is not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number 24K04912.

detail.abstract: Does diversity in ability and in mutual concern help or hurt team performance? We study a team in which efforts may be complements or substitutes. Holding mean ability and mean relational orientation fixed, we vary the dispersion of each. In horizontal teams, where no one leads, ability diversity raises performance through specialization regardless of the task, whereas diversity in relational orientation lowers it under complementarity and raises it under substitutability—so complementary tasks call for diverse hands but aligned hearts. Holding both attribute gaps fixed, performance is strictly higher when the abler member has the higher relational orientation, and the fully homogeneous team is a saddle point. In vertical teams, where one leads and the other follows, under weak interaction ability diversity remains beneficial regardless of who leads, while the optimal placement of the more prosocial member flips with the task—she should follow when efforts are complements and lead when they are substitutes. Taken together, the results show that the two dimensions of diversity interact and must be designed jointly rather than separately. Measuring relational orientation therefore pays off in both team composition and role assignment.

title: How Large Language Models Surface Personal Brands: An Entity-Signal Framework and Cross-System Analysis of ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: How Large Language Models Surface Personal Brands: An Entity-Signal Framework and Cross-System Analysis of ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity
detail.abstract: Professional discovery is migrating from ranked link lists to generated answers. When a prospect asks an assistant who the strongest expert in a category is, a large language model returns names, and the mechanism that decides which names appear is not the ranking logic that search engine optimization was built to influence. This paper introduces the AI Visibility Framework (AVF), a six-signal model of citation eligibility that governs whether a personal brand is retrieved, quoted, and recommended inside AI-generated answers across systems such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity. The six signals are web-wide reputation, source colocation, structured presence, distinctiveness, freshness, and crawl accessibility. Each signal is defined, assigned scoring criteria drawn from practitioner workflows, and weighted by its contribution to citation likelihood. The framework is grounded in entity-knowledge theory in large language models (Petroni et al., 2019; Kandpal et al., 2023) and in retrieval-augmented generation (Brown et al., 2020), and it extends the Personal Brand Equity Index (Sarkhedi, 2026a) by specifying the mechanism through which brand equity converts into machine visibility. Drawing on reported industry data compiled between December 2025 and June 2026, including a 527 percent yearover-year rise in AI referral traffic, the 60 percent of Google searches that end without a click, and the finding that 41 percent of AI-influenced conversions never appear in analytics, the paper argues that the relevant performance indicators shift from traffic to revenue, branded search, and cost per closed deal. A cross-system analysis shows that ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity weight sources differently, so visibility must be pursued one engine at a time. The framework is offered as a diagnostic tool for practitioners and as a research agenda for the emerging field of generative engine optimization.

title:
Play Smart, Not Hard: 
Disentangling the Impact of Expertise and Experience in Online Reviews
affiliations: ESSEC Business School,  and ESSEC Business School - Marketing Department

detail.title:
Play Smart, Not Hard: 
Disentangling the Impact of Expertise and Experience in Online Reviews
detail.abstract: Previous research on review helpfulness has so far given little attention to the impact of reviewer-specific characteristics such as product expertise and product experience. Past studies often conflated experience and expertise proxying both through the mere volume of previously authored reviews. This overlooks product-related expertise (demonstrated skill and proficiency) and product-related experience (accumulated product usage). Our research addresses this gap by conceptually and empirically disentangling the two constructs. Leveraging a dataset of 7.7 million reviews from Steam, we utilize precise, timestamped behavioral measures-playtime to capture experience, and in-game achievement completion to capture expertise. We replicate a U-shaped effect of reviewer experience on helpfulness, while revealing a strong, quasi-linear positive effect of reviewer expertise. We show that expertise exerts a significantly stronger influence on helpfulness than experience. We further demonstrate that these signals function as partial substitutes. Expertise matters most when experience is limited, with its marginal contribution diminishing as consumption time accumulates. Managerial simulations show that expertise-informed review curation strategies outperform experience-based approaches and increase average review helpfulness by up to 88%. Our findings offer a clear directive for managers, suggesting that review curation should not prioritize how long a reviewer has used the product, but how well.

title: Green Human Capital and Carbon Emissions of Asian Firms
affiliations: , IE Business School - IE University and Renmin University of China

detail.title: Green Human Capital and Carbon Emissions of Asian Firms

publicationDetails.detailsText: Asian Economic Policy Review, volume 21, issue 1, 2026[10.1111/aepr.70001]

detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of green human capital on corporate carbon emissions of Asian firms. Using firm-level carbon emission data and job posting data from 2009 to 2020, we find that a higher proportion of green job postings reduces firms' Scope 1 carbon emissions. This relationship holds across different seniority levels (junior and senior), and functional roles (managerial and technical). We leverage the staggered introduction of sustainability master programs to establish causality. Further analysis shows green human capital promotes both green innovation and renewable energy usage. These findings highlight the crucial role of green employees in driving corporate sustainability, offering policy insights for promoting low-carbon workforce strategies.

reference: Academic Journal of Social Sciences, volume 2, issue 2, 2026[10.21608/ajsc.2026.509699]
title: Future Jobs in Informational Crisis Management: A Hybrid Foresight based on Consumer Behavior Dynamics and Organizational Competencies
affiliations: Mansoura University, Mansoura University, Mansoura University and

detail.title: Future Jobs in Informational Crisis Management: A Hybrid Foresight based on Consumer Behavior Dynamics and Organizational Competencies

publicationDetails.detailsText: Academic Journal of Social Sciences, volume 2, issue 2, 2026[10.21608/ajsc.2026.509699]

detail.abstract:
Purpose: This study aims to anticipate and identify future job roles in marketing and human resource management through a quantitative analysis of complex interactions between consumer behavior (misinformation, FOMO, panic buying) and employee behavior (creative leadership, crisis management). 
The study adopts a hybrid methodological framework (SOBC-H) integrating Neutrosophic logic, fuzzy logic, artificial neural networks (ANN), and agent-based modeling (ABM).
Methodology: Data was derived from two previous research projects, collecting consumer data (N=637) and leader data (N=384) via electronic questionnaires. A Neutrosophic methodology was applied to transform Likert responses into triads (T, I, F), with the corresponding equations documented. Path analysis (SEM) was conducted to test direct and indirect effects, and moderation analysis was conducted to test the moderating role of misinformation. Two artificial neural networks were built to predict panic buying and crisis management efficiency, followed by ABM simulation across six functional scenarios.
Findings: Results revealed a substantial cognitive stability gap, with leaders showing a Deneutrosophicated weight (D=0.55) compared to consumers (D=0.50-0.53), reflecting a state of complete indeterminacy among consumers toward panic buying. Path analysis showed that the indirect effect of misinformation via FOMO (β=0.4399, p<0.001) is substantially stronger than its direct effect (β=0.0783, p=0.046). Moderation analysis revealed a significant interaction effect (β=0.0973, p=0.010). The ANN achieved R²=0.325 in predicting panic buying, while the creative leadership model achieved R²=0.860 in explaining crisis management efficiency. ABM simulation showed that synergy among the four proposed job roles achieves containment efficiency of up to 95% under ideal simulation conditions. Originality/Value: The research introduces the SOBC-H framework integrating behavioral profiling with computer simulation, with complete documentation of Neutrosophic transformation equations, and proposes four future job roles requiring technical (Python, SQL) and interactive (Digital Emotional Intelligence) competencies.

title: The Impact of Social Media Reels on Gen Z Travel Decisions
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Impact of Social Media Reels on Gen Z Travel Decisions
detail.abstract: As a recent high school graduate, I started paying attention to how my friends and I actually decide where to go on vacation. We don't look at travel brochures or TV commercials; we just scroll through TikTok and Instagram. This study explores how short-form videos, or reels, influence the travel plans of young people. I became interested in this topic after noticing how many travel destinations on my own social media feed were influencing where I wanted to travel inside and outside of Bangladesh. I surveyed 100 young adults to see what kind of videos catch their attention and who they trust. The results showed that almost everyone scored a 4.5 out of 5 or higher when asked if reels make them want to travel. The data suggests that we trust regular creators significantly more than official tourism boards, and that action sports and nature are what actually catch our eye.

title: Credit as Deferred Performance: An Institutional Theory of Credit Opening

detail.title: Credit as Deferred Performance: An Institutional Theory of Credit Opening
detail.abstract: This paper argues that credit is the institutional reality of deferred performance. Existing legal and economic accounts define credit through deferred payment, financial accommodation, claims, debt, purchasing power, balance-sheet expansion, or bank-created money, but they do not fully specify what is constituted at the moment of credit opening. The paper defines credit as a rule-constituted institutional relation across time in which performance is postponed, an obligation is opened, and closure is deferred. Credit opening produces a juridical claim-duty configuration: the creditor obtains a Deferred Performance Claim, while the debtor bears a Deferred Performance Duty. This configuration is the legal result of credit opening, not the ontology of credit itself. Loans, receivables, deposits, notes, bonds, and asset-liability pairs are accounting and financial expressions of deferred performance. The paper distinguishes credit from monetary closure: credit opens obligations, while money or institutionally empowered monetary proxies close them through recognized settlement. It contributes to institutional economics by defining credit not as an asset class, legal claim, or monetary substitute, but as deferred performance made institutionally real.

detail.abstract: Does language reshape what people eat? This paper identifies the causal effects of Mandarin proficiency and dialect distance on household food consumption in China, separating a humancapital "modernization channel" from a cultural-capital "local-network channel." Using three independent micro-datasets, the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS 2010 and 2014), the China Labor-force Dynamics Survey (CLDS 2014), and the China Health and Nutrition Survey (CHNS 1989-2015), we employ a three-layer identification strategy, with each layer relying on different identifying assumptions: two-stage least squares (2SLS) in the CFPS, instrumenting Mandarin proficiency with family language and county Mandarin share; an Atkin (2016)-style cross-dialect migrant design in the CHNS with community-by-wave fixed effects; and a bilingual dose-response analysis in the CLDS. Mandarin proficiency raises per-capita food expenditure by 13.85% and lowers animal-oil use, a pattern that replicates across datasets. Within the same community-year, cross-dialect migrants consume 0.93 fewer food types and 0.65 percentage points less protein energy than local residents and take roughly thirty years to assimilate; a 1989 direct-recall item shows that only 49.4% of cross-province migrants retain home foodways, against 90.7% of nonmigrants. We also report a cautionary null: province-level Mandarin penetration appears strongly correlated with dietary diversity but loses all significance once province fixed effects are added, signaling ecological-fallacy risk in cross-province studies. An Ashenfelter-Krueger correction further shows that the OLS-2SLS gap is partly classical measurement-error attenuation, with an implied reliability ratio of 0.27-0.66. Mandarin promotion thus accelerates dietary modernization while potentially eroding dialect-encoded local food knowledge, implying scope to coordinate language and nutrition policy under the "Greater Food Vision.

title: Ordering Bias and Ordering Variability: A Three-Step Approach for Interrater Reliability in Ordered Qualitative Coding
affiliations: FernUniversitat in Hagen, University of Melbourne, Universidad Politécnica de Madrid and University of Eastern Finland

detail.title: Ordering Bias and Ordering Variability: A Three-Step Approach for Interrater Reliability in Ordered Qualitative Coding
detail.abstract: Interrater reliability assessment in qualitative coding has historically focused on code detection and agreement regarding the presence of codes. Yet, numerous analytical methods depend on the sequence in which codes appear within an utterance. This paper makes three contributions. First, it introduces two metrics: ordering bias, which quantifies systematic directional disagreement in code placement, and ordering variability, which captures the dispersion of positional disagreement across utterances. Both metrics address the reliability of ordered coding schemes in which the relative position of codes carries substantive meaning. Second, both metrics are conditioned on detection agreement, isolating positional disagreement from detection disagreement at the level of individual codes. Combined with any binary detection metric, they constitute a three-step diagnostic framework for guiding the qualitative coding process and codebook development. Third, validation using synthetic data confirms that both metrics are bounded, symmetric around zero, and sensitive to known agreement conditions across realistic sample sizes.

detail.abstract: Over the past decade, the European Union has built a comprehensive supranational framework to combat corporate tax avoidance. This article provides the first integrated assessment of the EU's post-2015 anti-avoidance architecture, combining evidence on profit shifting by European multinationals, the effectiveness and side-effects of individual regulatory instruments, and the cumulative costs of tax complexity. While these measures have reduced specific profit-shifting channels, their marginal revenue impact appears limited relative to the rise in tax complexity, compliance costs, and distortions to investment, risk-taking, and innovation. The uneven global implementation of recent instruments-notably the Global Minimum Tax and public countryby-country reporting-has created a competitive asymmetry in which European multinationals bear regulatory burdens that their non-European competitors largely do not. The article concludes with policy recommendations to recalibrate the framework, eliminating rules whose marginal costs outweigh their marginal benefits while restoring the balance between enforcement and competitiveness that the EU's standard of "fair and efficient taxation" demands.

detail.abstract: This paper examines three landmark eminent domain cases, Poletown Neighborhood Council v. Detroit, County of Wayne v. Hathcock, and Kelo v. New London, which are often cited as evidence of inconsistent judicial outcomes. Using a comparative case analysis, it introduces Contextual Cost-Benefit Analysis (CCBA), a framework that interprets takings decisions as pragmatic evaluations in which costs and benefits are weighted by their contextual salience. The analysis shows that courts tend to uphold takings when projected benefits credibly outweigh the displacement and demoralization costs thereby generated, and reject them otherwise. This satisficing logic, grounded in Simon's concept of bounded rationality and North's account of institutional constraints, resembles the heuristic structure of the Hand rule in judicial reasoning rather than the marginal calculus of standard economic models. By identifying this distinct logic, CCBA suggests that accurate costbenefit analysis may require contextual weighting when decision-makers operate under institutional constraints.

title: Import Duty Pass-Through to Domestic Gold Prices: Quasi-Experimental Evidence from India's Gold Market, 2024-2026

detail.title: Import Duty Pass-Through to Domestic Gold Prices: Quasi-Experimental Evidence from India's Gold Market, 2024-2026
detail.abstract: This paper estimates how much of India's May 2026 gold import duty hike, from 6 to 15%, passed through to domestic gold prices. Exploiting the sharp and unanticipated policy discontinuity as a quasi-experiment, this paper applies an interrupted time series (ITS) design with Newey-West HAC standard errors to a primary sample of 375 daily observations from the India Bullion and Jewellers Association benchmark price series (July 2024-June 2026), with 346 pre-hike and 29 post-hike trading days. The full dataset comprises 929 daily price observations (824 IBJA PDF circulars and 105 BullionWorld.in gap-fills) spanning January 2022 through June 2026, within a 1,170-row weekday date spine. The duty hike raised the domestic gold premium by Rs. 9,841 per 10 grams, representing 81.7% of the theoretical ceiling, with a 95% confidence interval of 73.3 to 90.1%. Full passthrough is formally rejected (t =-4.26, p < 0.001). Local projections confirm the adjustment was immediate on the first trading day and held on a stable plateau through Day 14 (78.2%), with no evidence of anticipatory pricing. An ARDL bounds test confirms cointegration between domestic and international gold prices in the pre-hike period; the stable local-projection plateau through Day 14 is consistent with the shift persisting rather than mean-reverting within the observation window. Placebo tests and counterfactual methods confirm the result is specific to May 13, 2026. This paper also documents asymmetric price transmission: the duty hike passed through at 81.7% by the first trading day, while the July 2024 cut reached only 65.6% at an equivalent horizon (clean sample, July 2022-May 2026, N = 746). The hike therefore transmitted more completely than the cut, consistent with downward rigidity in duty pass-through. The incomplete pass-through is consistent with supply-side dampening from front-loaded inventory imported at the prior duty rate, seasonal demand weakness, and historical smuggling elasticity.

title: Does Public Procurement Select (Real) Outsider Innovation? The Interplay Between Tender Design and Supplier Experience

detail.title: Does Public Procurement Select (Real) Outsider Innovation? The Interplay Between Tender Design and Supplier Experience

publicationDetails.detailsText: ZEW - Centre for European Economic Research Discussion Paper No. 26-029
publicationDetails.journalName: ZEW - Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research Discussion Paper Series

publicationDetails.detailsText: ZEW – Centre for European Economic Research Discussion Paper No. 26-029

detail.abstract: Public organizations rely on open innovation to maintain and improve public service performance. Suppliers are a key source of such innovation. Public contracting authorities act as the interface between public organizations and supply markets, shaping whether supplier innovations are identified, rewarded, and selected. Combining representative firm-level data from the German Community Innovation Survey with official tender-level data from the Tenders Electronic Daily database, we construct firms' public procurement award histories between 2006 and 2023. We distinguish between four tender categories that differ by geographic scope (domestic versus international) and award mechanism (price-based versus criteria-based). We further differentiate between "real outsiders" and "pseudo-outsiders" based on experience supplying public markets. Using multivariate probit models, we examine how different degrees of innovation novelty are associated with supplier selection across tender categories and outsider status. Three findings emerge. i) Suppliers' category-specific procurement experience increases the likelihood of subsequent selection, indicating rigidity in public procurement markets. ii) Price-based tenders are associated with firm-level novelties, whereas criteria-based tenders are associated with market-specific novelties. iii) These innovation advantages are concentrated among "real outsiders" and largely disappear for "pseudo-outsiders", for whom prior category-specific procurement experience becomes the main predictor of subsequent selection.

title:
Getting the Vehicle Emissions Standard Right
How Canada can meet it s Climate and EV Adoption Goals

detail.title:
Getting the Vehicle Emissions Standard Right
How Canada can meet it s Climate and EV Adoption Goals
detail.abstract:
Multiple governments across the world are in the process of revising their light-duty vehicle emissions standards (VES) to achieve climate goals. Using Canada's vehicle emissions standard as an example, we examine the impact of multiple policy design options on GHG emissions, electric vehicle (EV) adoption, vehicle downsizing, and vehicle affordability. 
We find 
For Canada to meet its EV sales goal of 75% by 2035, it needs a VES target of 40 g/mile or lower. 
To reach its climate goals of 45% emissions reduction relative to 2005, Canada needs a more stringent VES target of 30 g/mile or lower by 2035.  
More stringent VES targets can contribute to additional price declines as automakers adjust pricing strategies and expand the availability of lower-cost EV models.  
A single fleet-wide VES target would be more effective at reducing emissions than maintaining separate targets for passenger cars and light trucks , as it would incentivize smaller and lighter vehicles .

keywords: empirical legal studies Right to Education

detail.abstract: How should internet-mediated public administration be evaluated when a statutory right depends on citizens finding, using, monitoring, and challenging a public-facing process? This article develops the construct of public observability: the extent to which a rights-claim pathway is publicly reconstructable through official digital and documentary interfaces. It applies the construct to Section 12(1)(c) of India’s Right to Education Act, which reserves at least 25 percent of entry-level seats in covered private unaided non-minority schools for eligible disadvantaged children. A multi-pass public-source audit of all 28 states and 8 union territories codes ten features across rules, portals, application routes, seat/school information, status tracking, results, guidance, helpdesks, grievance routes, and language/accessibility support. The study does not measure legal compliance, admissions, seat fill, parent experience, or usability; it asks whether a motivated public user or intermediary can reconstruct the claim pathway from official evidence. Results show bifurcation: 17 jurisdictions have High evidence confidence, two Medium, and 17 Low. Better-evidenced jurisdictions often make claim entry visible, but monitorability and contestability remain uneven. The article contributes a rights-pathway framework linking legal entitlement, public interface, claimability, monitorability, and contestability, and proposes minimum observability standards for digital-era rights implementation.

title: Measuring Consumption with Credit Card Data: Benchmarking and Beyond
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: Measuring Consumption with Credit Card Data: Benchmarking and Beyond
detail.abstract: We introduce a novel monthly county-level consumption dataset constructed from spending data on over 350 million credit cards in the Federal Reserve's Y-14M reports, covering over 3,000 U.S. counties since 2014. We first show that the data closely approximate traditional consumption measures, explaining 92 percent of the variation in monthly adjusted personal consumption expenditures (PCE) growth at the national level and capturing meaningful cross-sectional variation in annual adjusted PCE growth at the state level. As a proof of concept, we use the county-month panel to estimate heterogeneous consumption responses to monetary policy shocks across the county-level income distribution, an analysis infeasible with traditional consumption data. We find that low-income counties exhibit larger spending declines than high-income counties, consistent with heterogeneous agent New Keynesian models. Finally, we provide practical guidance for researchers working with similar data, discussing coverage, sample composition, and the approximation of credit card spending from credit bureau data.

title: People as the Source of Value A People-Centered Theory of Value and Economic Claims in the Data and Automation Age
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: People as the Source of Value A People-Centered Theory of Value and Economic Claims in the Data and Automation Age
detail.abstract: This paper advances a people-centered theory of economic value. Its central proposition is that in a data-driven and increasingly automated economy, people are not peripheral economic actors, nor merely consumers, workers, users, or one stakeholder group among many. They are the primary source from which economic value becomes possible. Every act of human participation, including purchase, attention, trust, loyalty, the generation of behavioural data, the expression of preference, and the sacrifice of alternative options, contributes to economic value. The question this paper addresses is therefore not whether participation creates value, which it takes to be evident, but how the value that people generate can be recognised, measured, recorded, and returned to its human source through an economically workable mechanism. The paper argues that the economic effects of human participation, including trust, consumption, labour, loyalty, attention, and behavioural data, already function as intangible value-bearing resources for firms. They contribute to revenue, brand value, customer retention, goodwill, acquisition premia, and the expectation of future cash flows. Yet existing economic and accounting frameworks permit firms to benefit from these people-generated intangibles while recognising no corresponding claim for the people whose conduct generates them. By analogy to the treatment of natural resources as common or national wealth, where an extracting firm earns a return on its capital, technology, and risk but does not thereby own the underlying resource, this paper argues that firms hold legitimate claims for the capital, organisation, processing, and risk they contribute, but not an automatic and exclusive claim over the whole of the value generated from human participation. This framework is named PAYMAN, standing for People As Your MANdate, denoting the proposition that people, through their participation, hold a mandate over the value they make possible. The paper formalises a set of conditions under which participation-based value can be operationally recognised and repaid, proposes an extension to the accounting identity that records people-generated intangible assets alongside a corresponding participation claim, and introduces the concept of a value flow, distinct from cash flow, together with a secondary market in which participation-based claims could be exchanged. PAYMAN is presented as a foundational theory for a new economic architecture rather than as an already operational system; its empirical calibration and legal development are identified as a research agenda.
