title: LLM-Powered Virtual Population for Demand Simulation and Pricing
affiliations: and

detail.title: LLM-Powered Virtual Population for Demand Simulation and Pricing
detail.abstract: We develop an LLM-powered virtual population model that simulates demand for pricing decisions, in settings where products are described by rich unstructured information, such as text descriptions and images, and where decision makers need not only mean-demand predictions but also uncertainty estimates for counterfactual prices. Our model represents exposed customers as draws from a finite mixture of customer personas. For each persona, product, and candidate price, an LLM elicits a persona-level purchase probability using both structured persona information and unstructured product information. These probabilities are aggregated through calibrated mixture weights to form a predictive distribution of aggregate demand. The resulting simulator can evaluate counterfactual prices under various pricing objectives, including expected revenue and risk-aware criteria such as conditional value at risk. We test the framework on an online H&M fashion dataset with product descriptions and images. The calibrated LLM-based simulator achieves the best overall predictive performance among the models considered, and supports sample-efficient pricing decisions. Our framework provides a practical way to use LLMs as demand simulators for products with limited historical demand data but rich product information. By producing a full predictive demand distribution rather than only a point forecast, it enables managers to compare candidate prices, quantify demand uncertainty, and choose prices that target either average-case revenue or risk-aware objectives.

title: Incorporating Price Limits into Deep Learning for Stock Return Prediction in the Chinese A-Share Market
affiliations: and

detail.title: Incorporating Price Limits into Deep Learning for Stock Return Prediction in the Chinese A-Share Market
detail.abstract: Daily price limits in the Chinese A-share market impose regulatory bounds on observed daily stock returns, producing a truncated return distribution in which limit-hit observations are censored realizations of a latent return. Standard deep learning models ignore the bounded nature of observed returns and treat all observations as uncensored in the loss function. This paper proposes two components to address this limitation: a bounded sigmoid output layer that constrains predictions to the feasible return interval, and a Student-t Tobit loss function that treats limit-hit observations as censored realizations of a latent return. The two components are evaluated in an ablation framework across four architectures (MLP, LSTM, TCN, and Transformer) on the full Chinese A-share universe from 2019 to 2026. The results show that the bounded output layer helps cross-sectional ranking on limit-hit observations specifically, but does not improve overall performance on its own. The Student-t Tobit loss improves cross-sectional ranking performance over the MSE baseline in three out of four architectures, with the largest gain for MLP (Rank IC from 0.0390 to 0.0666), driven primarily by better performance on non-limit observations. When the two components are combined, performance improves over the baseline in all four architectures, though the combined method does not consistently surpass the Tobit loss alone.

title: Abel-Regularized Volterra Solvers for American Option Free Boundaries
affiliations: Department of Mathematics

detail.title: Abel-Regularized Volterra Solvers for American Option Free Boundaries

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF-2019R1I1A3A03059382) and BK21 FOUR (No. 5120200913674).

detail.abstract: We present a computational framework for single-and coupled Americanstyle free-boundary problems governed by nonlinear weakly singular Volterra integral equations. The free boundary is parameterized using B-splines, reducing the global continuous problem to a low-dimensional residual system in coefficient space. An Abel-type product-integration scheme regularizes the local near-diagonal Volterra scaling, yielding a consistent residual quadrature and a well-scaled Jacobian assembly. The system is solved via a residualcorrection iteration using a hierarchy of automatic-differentiation-based full Jacobians and computationally efficient reduced Jacobian models. Numerical experiments on American puts, dividend-paying calls, and coupled choosertype contracts across standard and challenging parameter regimes demonstrate stable boundary reconstruction, accurate prices, and computational efficiency.

title: Quiet Booms, Sudden Stops: The Volatility Credit Nexus
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, The University of Hong Kong and The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: Quiet Booms, Sudden Stops: The Volatility Credit Nexus
detail.abstract: Sudden stops are typically preceded by low volatility in both advanced and emerging market economies. Low volatility is an effective predictor of sudden stops, even after controlling for credit and growth. Moreover, a credit boom associated with low volatility is significantly more likely to end in a sudden stop. To account for these facts, we develop a quantitative model with recursive utility, stochastic volatility in productivity trends, and an occasionally binding loan-to-value credit constraint. The model replicates the dynamic patterns among volatility, credit and sudden stops in the data. Low volatility inflates the price of collateral, reduces concerns about a future binding constraint, and encourages borrowing. We show that both recursive preferences and stochastic volatility of trend shocks are essential for the collateral price effect of volatility.

title: The Economics of Regulating Tokenized Securities
affiliations: University of Oxford,  and University of Florida

detail.title: The Economics of Regulating Tokenized Securities
detail.abstract: We develop an economic model to study the effect of regulation on tokenized securities markets. Tokenizing a security does not exempt it from securities laws, so in our framework token issuers must choose a compliance policy that restricts trading. We characterize the resulting trade-off between regulatory stringency and financial market outcomes, and we derive three main results. First, tighter regulation reduces the liquidity of the tokenized market. Second, tokenization is not commercially viable for sufficiently strict regulation. Third, the tightest level of regulation that tokenization can withstand depends on the characteristics of the tokenized asset.

title: Uninitiated Obligation: Fictitious Capital, Deferred Labour, and Who Pays When It Ends
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Uninitiated Obligation: Fictitious Capital, Deferred Labour, and Who Pays When It Ends
detail.abstract: When a speculative price collapses, neoclassical theory says the lost value evaporates, and Minsky says it was transferred along the chain of prior transactions. Neither answer says what the lost quantity is. This paper argues, strictly within the labour theory of value, that the portion of a speculative price unanchored by completed production is an obligation whose substance is labour. To capitalise a claim on future surplus value is necessarily to presuppose the constant and variable capital of a production cycle that has not been initiated. From this single mechanism, the stuffing of an entire future commodity value W′ into present price, the paper derives the interior structure of the gap between price and value, the reason fictitious capital persists as long as it does and no longer, and the exact set of channels through which the obligation is redistributed when its container fails. The framework answers three questions Marx left open and states the conditions under which it would be false.

title: The Illusion of Competence: Title Inflation, Juniorization, and the Crisis in Cybersecurity Governance and ICT Auditing
affiliations: Cybersecurity Advisor & Implementor

detail.abstract: The global cybersecurity and ICT auditing ecosystem faces a critical structural crisis driven by the convergence of an acute talent shortage, aggressive corporate budget retrenchments, and the systematic juniorization of complex assurance roles. This paper provides a multidimensional analysis of the cybersecurity labor market, examining how unrealistic job descriptions, title inflation, and a cost-arbitrage-driven outsourcing model have compromised the integrity of ICT audits and cybersecurity governance. By contrasting hiring practices in India with those in the United States, the paper analyzes the experience disconnect, the credentialing arms race, the commoditization of governance, risk, and compliance functions through tool-centric hiring, and the resulting failure of policy and control design. It further examines the impact on audit quality, including checklist auditing, checklist fatigue, loss of professional skepticism, and the dangerous state of compliance illusion. The paper concludes with a framework for realigning expectations and restoring integrity to cybersecurity audit practice.

title: The Role of Ecosystem Services in Supporting Rural Livelihoods Around Old Oyo National Park, Nigeria
affiliations: Federal University of Technology, Akure and Federal University of Technology Akure (FUTA)

detail.title: The Role of Ecosystem Services in Supporting Rural Livelihoods Around Old Oyo National Park, Nigeria
detail.abstract: Ecosystem services play a critical role in supporting rural livelihoods, particularly in communities located around protected areas where dependence on natural resources remains high. This study examined the contribution of ecosystem services to rural livelihood sustainability in communities adjoining Old Oyo National Park, Nigeria. Specifically, the study identified key ecosystem resources utilized by local communities and assessed their importance in supporting household livelihoods and socioeconomic well-being. Primary data were collected through the administration of 384 structured questionnaires among residents of selected support-zone communities surrounding the park using a multistage sampling technique. Data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistical methods. The findings revealed that respondents derived significant livelihood benefits from ecosystem services provided by the park. Major ecosystem resources identified included fauna resources (80.7%), flora resources (78.6%), fertile land (76.3%), medicinal plants (70.1%), clean water (59.6%), grassland resources (59.9%), and cultural relics (54.4%). Respondents further considered bush meat, bush food, medicinal plants, water resources, and hunting activities as highly important for household sustenance and income generation. The results demonstrate the strong dependence of rural households on ecosystem services for food security, healthcare, employment, and environmental sustainability. The study concludes that ecosystem services provided by Old Oyo National Park contribute significantly to rural livelihood resilience and community welfare. Consequently, conservation policies should 2 integrate biodiversity protection with livelihood improvement strategies to ensure sustainable resource management and long-term ecosystem sustainability.

title: The Objective Fetish: Reflexivity, Behaviour Homomorphism, and the Material Termination of Speculative Regimes
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Objective Fetish: Reflexivity, Behaviour Homomorphism, and the Material Termination of Speculative Regimes
detail.abstract: Speculative regimes persist longer than arbitrage should allow and terminate at moments their participants do not anticipate. The dominant explanations, reflexivity and narrative economics, are idealist in structure: the regime is sustained by belief and ends when belief reverses, which explains the reversal by the reversal. This paper supplies the objective floor those accounts lack, by an explicitly dialectical and materialist method. Soros's two functions, the cognitive and the participating, are re-grounded asymmetrically through Lenin's theory of reflection: consciousness reflects an objective base it does not constitute and acts back upon it only within finite material means, so the reflexive loop acquires a floor. Persistence rests on a behavioural mechanism, Behaviour Homomorphism, a structure-preserving map carrying heterogeneous priors onto uniform behaviour while preserving the priors it confirms, grounded in one organism and environment contradiction at two strata and given content by the value-form, the M-M′ fetish in which the production circuit is obscured. The market, a selective environment, sweeps the population toward a behavioural monoculture fitted to price and unfit for realisation. Termination is the reassertion of the base, through the one layer the sweep cannot reach, the liquidity selected on repayment. The paper is ontological.

title:
Derivatives Clearing: A Comprehensive Guide 
Risk Management, Regulation, and the Future of the Markets (Introduction and Chapter 1)

detail.title:
Derivatives Clearing: A Comprehensive Guide 
Risk Management, Regulation, and the Future of the Markets (Introduction and Chapter 1)
detail.abstract:
Derivatives are indispensable to modern finance, yet the infrastructure that makes them safe to trade at scale remains under-researched. The over-the-counter derivatives market alone exceeds USD 700 trillion in notional outstanding (BIS, 2023), and every trade within it depends on a finely engineered sequence of execution, clearing, and settlement. This book offers a comprehensive, systematic, and practice-oriented account of the pivotal phase within that sequence: clearing—the mechanism by which a central counterparty (CCP) interposes itself between the parties to a trade, assumes counterparty risk, and guarantees performance.

While excellent references exist on derivative products, pricing, and market risk, works that treat clearing itself systematically—its mechanics, risk management, regulation, and recent evolution—have remained scarce, particularly in Japanese. This book aims to fill that gap. It locates clearing within the trade lifecycle; explains the roles of CCPs, clearing brokers, and clients; and rigorously analyzes the core risk-management apparatus: initial and variation margin (SPAN® and VaR-based models, MPOR, procyclicality), the default waterfall, stress testing, and default auctions. It surveys the regulatory framework that emerged from the post-2008 G20 reforms—the CPMI-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures, Dodd-Frank, EMIR, and Japan's Financial Instruments and Exchange Act—and the practical realities of client onboarding and documentation. It concludes with an investigation into the evolutionary trajectory of client clearing: sponsored access, direct clearing, the convergence with prime brokerage, and the transformative impact of DLT and AI.

Throughout, clearing is treated not as back-office processing but as critical market infrastructure—an intellectually demanding, strategic discipline whose design determines where risk concentrates and how market stability is preserved.

title: Valuation Multiples in U.S. HVAC Service Businesses: A Synthesis of Tiered Pricing, Recurring-Revenue Premia, and Buyer-Archetype Differentiation in the Lower Middle Market

detail.title: Valuation Multiples in U.S. HVAC Service Businesses: A Synthesis of Tiered Pricing, Recurring-Revenue Premia, and Buyer-Archetype Differentiation in the Lower Middle Market

detail.abstract: This paper provides a structured synthesis of valuation-multiple evidence for U.S. heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) service businesses in the lower middle market. Drawing on publicly-disclosed transaction data, SEC 10-K filings of publicly-traded HVAC consolidators (Comfort Systems USA, EMCOR Group, Watsco), practitioner valuation reports, and the academic literature on private-company acquisition pricing, the synthesis documents five empirical patterns. First, valuation multiples exhibit a strong size-tier gradient: businesses with under one million dollars in Seller's Discretionary Earnings (SDE) typically transact at 2.0 to 3.0 times SDE through SBA-financed individual-buyer channels, while businesses with twenty-five million dollars or more of trailing EBITDA have transacted in 2024–2026 at platform-level multiples in the 13 to 20 times range, indicated by press-derived references for transactions including the November 2024 Sila Services and February 2026 Champions Group transactions. The transition from SDE-based to EBITDA-based valuation at approximately one million dollars in annual owner economic benefit is identified as a discontinuous threshold rather than a smooth gradient. Second, recurring-revenue intensity is associated with material multiple expansion: practitioner reporting consistently identifies an additional 0.5 to 1.0 times EBITDA premium for HVAC businesses with thirty percent or more revenue from maintenance-agreement membership programmes, with a structural floor at the 2.0 to 3.0 times annual-recurring-revenue valuation level for plan portfolios considered standalone. Third, buyer-archetype differentiates achievable price: PE platform sponsors, PE add-on capital, search funders, family offices, and strategic acquirers exhibit distinguishable multiple ranges and cash-versus-rollover-versus-earnout deal-structure preferences. Fourth, observable value-driver characteristics (geographic concentration in the Sun Belt, commercial versus residential revenue mix, management depth, owner-dependency, fleet age, license-holder structure, customer concentration) compress or expand multiples within the size-tier band by margins documented in practitioner reporting. Fifth, the academic literature on private-company acquisition discounts (Officer, 2007) provides theoretical grounding for the directional pattern that LMM private HVAC transaction multiples remain below the multiples of publicly-traded mechanical-services consolidators; the magnitude of the gap, however, cannot be cleanly attributed to the Officer mechanism alone, because the available listed comparables (Comfort Systems USA, EMCOR Group, Watsco) differ from the Tier 5 private platforms by approximately one order of magnitude in EBITDA scale, by material business-mix composition, and by cycle-specific data-centre construction demand exposure. The synthesis is situated within the academic literature on buy-and-build value creation (Hammer, Marcotty-Dehm, Schweizer, & Schwetzler, 2022; Heisig, Kick, & Schwetzler, 2022) and the empirical literature on industry consolidation. Acknowledged limitations include the absence of audited deal-level multiple data at the LMM-private-transaction level, the practitioner-aggregated source character of the size-tier and buyer-archetype pricing ranges, and the U.S.-centric scope.

title: The U.S. HVAC Private-Equity Consolidation Cycle (2018-2026): An Empirical Case Study in Platform Formation, Multiple Expansion, and Late-Cycle Transition

detail.abstract: The U.S. residential and commercial heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) services industry has experienced one of the most extensively documented private-equity (PE) consolidation cycles of the past decade. This paper provides an empirical case-study synthesis of that cycle, drawing on publicly-disclosed platform-formation events, sponsor press releases, SEC filings of publicly-traded consolidators, and the academic literature on buy and-build strategies. The synthesis is organised around three observable cycle stages applied to the U.S. HVAC industry: an early-cycle platform-formation window (2016–2019), a mid-cycle add-on-acquisition expansion (2019–2023), and a late-cycle transition (2024–2026) characterised by consolidator-of consolidator transactions, secondary-market platform recapitalisations, and the emergence of a structural divergence between the residential and commercial sub-segments. Five platform-level cap-table transactions closed in the eighteen months preceding this paper (Sila Services to Goldman Sachs Alternatives in November 2024, Apex Service Partners 3.4 billion dollar single asset continuation in May 2025, Redwood Services to Altas Partners at approximately 1.1 billion dollars in May 2025, Service Logic to Bain Capital and Mubadala in December 2025, and Champions Group to Blackstone BXPE in February 2026), and a sixth (a strategic minority investment in Apex Service Partners by Apollo Funds) was announced May 28, 2026 with closing expected in Q4 2026, together documenting the late-cycle dynamic with particular clarity. Three synthesis results are reported. First, the U.S. HVAC industry remains substantially fragmented at the establishment level (approximately 50,000 to 100,000 independently owned operators, with IBISWorld 2026 reporting industry revenue of 159.4 billion U.S. dollars), but the active count of named PE-backed and publicly-traded consolidators (27 or more identified, per practitioner inventory in Capstone Partners, 2025), the ubiquity of trade-press coverage of consolidation as a defining industry theme, and the platform-level transaction trajectory documented in Section 4 together place the industry in the late-cycle stage on the operational signals derived from the industry-life cycle tradition (Klepper, 1996, 1997) and the buy-and-build empirical literature (Hammer et al., 2022; Heisig et al., 2022). Second, the residential and commercial sub-segments are diverging in cycle stage and value-creation mechanics, with residential exhibiting consolidator-of-consolidator dynamics and modest multiple compression while commercial HVAC remains in mid cycle expansion driven by data-center demand and mission-critical preventative-maintenance contract economics. Third, the 2024–2025 regulatory transition from R-410A to A2L refrigerants (with refrigerant input cost increases of approximately six-fold and technician recertification requirements) is acting as an asymmetric structural tailwind to consolidation by raising the fixed-cost barrier to small-operator viability. The synthesis is situated within the academic literature on buy-and-build returns and multiple arbitrage (Hammer, Marcotty-Dehm, Schweizer, & Schwetzler, 2022; Heisig, Kick, & Schwetzler, 2022) and the industry-life-cycle tradition originating with Gort and Klepper (1982). Limitations include the inability to observe non disclosed transactions, the absence of audited cross-deal multiple data at the platform level, and the U.S.-centric scope.

title: Atomic Finance: The Quiet Alchemy of Modern Markets
affiliations: Regional Advisory Commision on Financial Markets

detail.title: Atomic Finance: The Quiet Alchemy of Modern Markets
detail.abstract:
In tiny moments of trade, the economy breathes its next instant. Purchase orders fill one half of the order book, as sell orders drain the other half. These transactions have negligible size relative to the scales of the world, are saturated in nuance and subtlety, and unfold at a furious tempo, the air crackling with their soundless symphony.

For most markets and ecosystems, these fleeting seconds coalesce into an economic pulse with shape, colour, touch, and smell. It carries wear, rhythm, and often the response of a dawn chorus. In sharp contrast, traditional finance relegates its humming ecology to distant whispers. Cancelling the noise altogether renders play and expression invisible, yet they still lie at the heart of the economy's evolution. A market transforms the tiny world into poetry; the tiny world, softly, stillness; the score of evolution, heartbeat. Emotion in numbers has always inspired artists, and these artists continue their work, now with the tools of precision finance.

Atomic finance creates a quiet instrument of strange, resonant beauty. Market microstructure becomes pure data, a fine-grained record of player behaviours. The departure from conventional finance lies largely in a reversal of tradition: transparency and trust create precise data; precise data become credible risks; credible risks govern reward. It is a gentle, peaceful evolution, yielding deep, colourful maps of the tiny world's poem.

title: Sovereign Logistics, Absent Diplomacy: Azerbaijan, the Silent Keystone of ASEAN–Europe Supply Chain Connectivity
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Sovereign Logistics, Absent Diplomacy: Azerbaijan, the Silent Keystone of ASEAN–Europe Supply Chain Connectivity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This research received no external funding. The author is an independent researcher. The views expressed are solely those of the author.

detail.abstract: The European Union has committed €22 billion to the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR), the United States is reported to hold approximately 74% of the development company building its new Armenian bypass, and Singapore's state-owned port operator is physically present in its Azerbaijani hub. ASEAN — whose manufactured goods can enter the Chongqing–TITR circuit and thereby transit Azerbaijan en route to European markets — has not formally engaged Azerbaijan in any connectivity instrument. This paper introduces the concept of the silent keystone — a transit state that has acquired structural corridor significance before receiving formal diplomatic recognition from the corridor's principal origin or destination regions — and argues that Azerbaijan is the current exemplar. Four necessary conditions, derived inductively from Djibouti, Panama, and Singapore, are applied to Azerbaijan and tested against three negative cases: Georgia (recognised, not silent), Kyrgyzstan (not yet consequential), and Belarus on the pre-2022 Northern Corridor (recognised by the EU, its corridor's destination region). The paper documents that ASEAN has engaged the corridor's Chinese origination point (full Dialogue Partner), its eastern land anchor — Singapore, an ASEAN member state, engaged Kazakhstan bilaterally through the 2025 S&I Agreement naming the TITR — and its western European terminus (Turkey, Sectoral Dialogue Partner since 2017), but not the mandatory Caspian crossing. An inventory-carrying-cost model shows the corridor generates approximately US$6,048 per FEU net advantage for integrated circuit shipments at nominal transit time. For the semiconductor sub-category of EU-Asia trade — the supply chain most exposed to Hormuz closure — the corridor's infrastructure capacity is sufficient to accommodate 5% Operational Presence diversification for this sub-category, though the semiconductor-specific share of current TITR throughput is not publicly disaggregated. ASEAN's silence on Azerbaijan is most analytically strange for the sub-category where the recognition would matter most — and where the window for first-mover recognition is narrowing not because Azerbaijan's position is fragile, but because the corridor's significance is becoming too apparent to generate pioneering diplomatic value.

detail.abstract: The persistent problem of managing the Medium of Instruction (MoI) in multilingual tertiary institutions lies in the tension between policy uniformity and classroom realities, which often results in gaps in comprehension and students engagement. This study aimed to explore how a state-owned institution managed its MoI, focusing on enforcement, adaptation, and alignment. Anchored in Spolsky's Language Policy Framework (2004), the research employed a qualitative single-case study design, with the institution as the case and five faculty members from different academic institutes and five students of different courses. Results revealed that teachers enforced the MoI through governance structures, compliance tools, and national mandates; they adapted through code-switching, translation, scaffolding, and multimodal strategies validated by students; and a misalignment persisted between institutional language policies and multilingual classroom practices, affecting students' socio-emotional confidence and participation. These findings imply that policy must move beyond rigid enforcement toward context-responsive multilingualism, integrating flexible strategies that acknowledge diverse linguistic repertoires. By aligning institutional mandates with classroom realities, language policy could foster inclusivity, strengthen learner confidence, and ensure equitable access to knowledge across disciplines.

title: Energy's Blue Footprint: Assessing Corporate Liability and Regulatory Gaps in Marine Pollution
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Energy's Blue Footprint: Assessing Corporate Liability and Regulatory Gaps in Marine Pollution
detail.abstract: This article examines the intersection of corporate liability and regulatory architecture in addressing marine pollution generated by the global energy sector. Through doctrinal analysis of international treaty frameworks including UNCLOS, MARPOL, and the OSPAR Convention and comparative evaluation of national legal regimes in Nigeria and the United Kingdom, the article identifies systemic gaps in the operationalisation of the Polluter Pays Principle as a binding corporate accountability standard. Four recent developments structure the analysis: the ITLOS Advisory Opinion on Climate Change and International Law (2024), the just transition imperative and its implications for marine environmental restitution, the absence of a dedicated marine supplement to Nigeria's Petroleum Industry Act 2021, and the Deepwater Horizon federal consent decree as a template for comprehensive corporate accountability. The article concludes with a five-part reform programme anchored in a reconstituted regulatory compact that treats ecological restoration, unjust enrichment disgorgement, and community just transition as standard accountability outcomes rather than exceptional remedies.

title: Financial Awareness and Budgetary Decision-Making Patterns Among Uzbekistan's Youth: A Quantitative Analysis of Consumer Financial Literacy
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Unaffiliated Author

detail.title: Financial Awareness and Budgetary Decision-Making Patterns Among Uzbekistan's Youth: A Quantitative Analysis of Consumer Financial Literacy
detail.abstract: This research paper examines the current state of financial literacy and budgetary decision-making among the youth in Uzbekistan through a quantitative analysis of primary survey data (n = 50+). The study focuses on five critical pillars of financial awareness: understanding of inflation, ability to calculate interest, budgeting habits, barriers to investment, and the prevailing preference for physical cash. The findings reveal a significant reliance on cash-based savings (63%), a strong prioritization of education as the most meaningful investment (50%), and a pervasive desire for enhanced economic education within the formal school curriculum. While a majority of respondents demonstrate a partial to good understanding of inflation (73% combined), a substantial portion (43%) remains hesitant in applying practical financial skills such as interest calculation. Drawing on community-level primary data and corroborated by national and international reports, this paper provides empirical evidence to support policy recommendations aimed at bridging the gap between theoretical financial knowledge and practical wealth management among the younger demographic in Uzbekistan.

title: How to Calculate China's Gradually Transitional Economy: A Study based on Endogenous Institutional Variables

detail.title: How to Calculate China's Gradually Transitional Economy: A Study based on Endogenous Institutional Variables
detail.abstract: China is a gradually transitioning country with continuously changing institutions, which inevitably affect the output and growth of its national economy. However, mainstream economic growth models all assume that institutions remain unchanged and cannot accurately calculate a national economy characterized by the long-term coexistence of a dual institutional system. The author uses distribution proportions and state efficiency as fundamental institutional variables, viewing outcomes under market economy influence as standard values and those under planned administrative influence as distortion values. Based on this, two foundational formulas are first established, upon which the output function and growth model of China's gradually transitional economy are constructed according to mathematical economic logic. This model is then used to explain China's past growth miracle and to forecast future economic growth, offering ideas for institutional reforms in key areas.

title: Strengthening Project Preparation for Subnational Climate Finance in Africa: A Systems and Operations Management Approach

detail.title: Strengthening Project Preparation for Subnational Climate Finance in Africa: A Systems and Operations Management Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A

detail.abstract:
While the barriers to mobilising climate and infrastructure finance in Africa are well recognised, less understood is how weaknesses in the enabling environment and early-stage project preparation contribute to low project bankability and limited climate finance mobilisation at the subnational level. This study applies a user-centric, systems-thinking approach to examine the subnational climate finance gap in Africa, exploring how project preparation facilities (PPFs) can more effectively support cities in developing bankable climate infrastructure projects and accessing climate finance. 

The research shifts the analytical lens from the supply side, i.e. donor governments, multilateral development banks and global facilities towards the demand side, i.e. cities and project sponsors. Drawing on insights from municipal governments, PPF managers, development finance institutions, development agencies and technical advisors, the study develops a novel taxonomy of upstream subnational, urban and climate-focused PPFs. This framework enables bottlenecks to be analysed across facility models and project lifecycle stages, providing a structured basis for identifying where constraints converge and prioritising interventions. 

The findings identify four interconnected bottlenecks constraining climate finance mobilisation: 

(i) demand-side constraints relating to local capacity and absorptive readiness; 

(ii) supply-side constraints arising from fragmented PPF mandates, funding structures and support models; 

(iii) demand-side creditworthiness and trust constraints that limit municipal engagement with financiers; 

and (iv) system-level constraints driven by vertical misalignment between national and subnational actors and downward risk transfer due to fragmented capital sources characterising blended finance. 

The study finds that these challenges are largely systemic, affecting numerous diverse PPF models, rather than facility-specific, and disproportionately affect secondary and intermediary cities. It concludes that improving climate finance mobilisation requires coordinated reforms across demand-side, supply-side and system-level actors, alongside stronger alignment between PPFs, national governments and cities to create more investable, climate-aligned infrastructure pipelines.

title: Regime Representation and Base Forecaster Selection in Conformal VaR: What Actually Drives Calibration Quality
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Regime Representation and Base Forecaster Selection in Conformal VaR: What Actually Drives Calibration Quality

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. No financial relationships with organizations that could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. All data used are publicly available (Yahoo Finance, FRED).

detail.abstract: We ask which of the two core design choices in conformal Value-at-Risk-the base forecaster or the calibration kernel-is first-order for Bear-regime calibration quality. Using N = 2,113 daily test observations across four ETFs (SPY, QQQ, TLT, GLD) from January 2018 through June 2026, we find that the base forecaster dominates. Replacing Historical Simulation (HS) with Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (GBDT) eliminates Bear-period exceedance clustering on equity assets across all kernel specifications: the SPY Bear-period clustering ratio falls from 12.29× under HS to 1.01× under GBDT, and the Ljung-Box Q(10) statistic on the Bear-regime conformity score series falls by 25× on SPY and 59× on QQQ. The calibration kernel is second-order: under a controlled comparison, an HMM-posterior kernel using Jensen-Shannon divergence and a realized-volatility Euclidean kernel produce identical Bear-period exceedance rates at all calibration window lengths tested (m cal ∈ {63, 126, 252, 504} trading days), despite encoding informationally distinct signals (ρ = 0.103). The mechanism is recency decay: the time-decay term e-λ(t-i) dominates the cross-sectional kernel geometry at standard window lengths, rendering kernel choice coverage-neutral. The base-forecaster advantage is equity-specific: on TLT and GLD, where tail dynamics are driven by rate shocks and commodity flows orthogonal to equity-momentum features, HS and GBDT produce similar clustering ratios. We connect these findings to regime-conditional tail-risk pricing [Dai, 2026], where the Bear-regime CF-CVaR interaction coefficient is λ3 =-0.046 (t =-2.43): HS systematically understates Bear-period tail exposure precisely when the market prices tail risk most aggressively, and GBDT eliminates that understatement on equity assets.

title: Asymmetric Coexistence Theory: Governance-Aware Certification of Non-Capturing Assistance
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Asymmetric Coexistence Theory: Governance-Aware Certification of Non-Capturing Assistance

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it is a theoretical and conceptual research paper and did not involve human participants, patients, animals, personal data, clinical data, interviews, surveys, or case studies requiring consent.

detail.abstract: Future intelligent societies will contain persistent relations among unequally capable agents, institutions, artificial systems, collective agents, represented future constituencies, and adaptive systems. Assistance in such relations can be valuable, but it can also become capturing: it may improve immediate performance while reducing the assisted party's future capacity to understand, refuse, repair, learn, contest, exit, recover, form values, generate independent descriptions of its world, or act before irreversible branches close. This paper develops Asymmetric Coexistence Theory (ACT) as a theory of certifiable non-capturing assistance. The minimal ACT kernel consists of a typed agency space, an asymmetric regime, an admissible baseline, a counterfactual agency estimand, a debt-and-recoverability account, and a certification claim. Additional modules handle semantic generation, temporal asymmetry, successor identity, graphinternal audit, recursive certification bases, adaptive challenge evidence, certification-governance capture, runtime agency hazards, non-dominating enforcement, specification validity, model uncertainty, historical baseline corruption, coalitional pressure, scarce certification resources, multi-scale composition, and stochastic capture risk. The main contribution is to treat practical certification as a runtime assurance case rather than as an omniscient proof of autonomy. An ACT certificate states its claim, scope, tier, assumptions, evidence, argument, defeaters, residual risk, and revalidation triggers, and it gives a graph semantics for how evidence supports claims and how unresolved defeaters attack them. Because asymmetric relations change after certification, the certificate also has a lifecycle state, monitorable claims, evidence freshness bounds, tamper-evident audit traces, disclosed certification bases, challenge portfolios, adaptive evaluation budgets, certification-governance records, agency-hazard tables, enforcement authority maps, and fallback obligations when certification is suspended, expired, or invalidated. Exact viability kernels remain ideal objects; deployed certification is a conservative sufficient claim whose measurement validity, causal identification, evidence provenance, baseline comparability, audit independence, audit capacity, verifier cost, proof coverage, proxy validity, nonlinear error envelope, model ambiguity, shared-resource feasibility, compositional scope, recursive support discipline, runtime enforcement boundary, challenge coverage, challenge exposure, certifier independence, and stochastic margin must be explicit. Human-AI capability atrophy remains an important example, but the theory is formulated for asymmetric intelligent coexistence in general.

title: Autocatalytic Foreclosure: A Structural Theory of Institutional Revision Failure
affiliations: Institutional Adaptation Partners LLC

detail.title: Autocatalytic Foreclosure: A Structural Theory of Institutional Revision Failure
detail.abstract: Institutions do not fail because they cannot decide. They fail because they cannot revise what they have already decided. This paper introduces autocatalytic foreclosure as a structural theory of institutional revision failure. Drawing on Charlat et al.'s 2025 PNAS model of autocatalytic closure in chemical systems as a structural analogue, the paper argues that institutional decision frameworks become self-reinforcing through recursive validation loops -- processes by which prior commitments generate the evidentiary and procedural conditions that confirm those commitments. Once closure is reached, the institution loses functional revision capacity not because actors are irrational or information is absent, but because the architecture of the decision system structurally excludes revision as a viable output. The paper formalizes the closure mechanism, identifies its structural preconditions, distinguishes autocatalytic foreclosure from adjacent concepts in organizational theory, and specifies the architectural conditions under which revision capacity is preserved. The analysis has direct implications for intelligence community analytic tradecraft, corporate governance, public sector institutional design, and organizational resilience.

title: Structural-Break Entry and the Disposition Effect in a Commercial XAUUSD Strategy: A Tick-Level Decomposition
affiliations: , Jinan University and Jinan University

detail.title: Structural-Break Entry and the Disposition Effect in a Commercial XAUUSD Strategy: A Tick-Level Decomposition

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The trading strategy evaluated in this study is under active commercial deployment, and the first author (Yongjun Quan) is associated with its operation. The first author received no payment for conducting this research, and all authors report no other competing financial or personal interests. The study includes negative findings that run counter to the strategy's commercial framing, reflecting the authors' commitment to an unbiased assessment.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants or animals. It is based solely on historical market price data; therefore, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Technical trading strategies combine entry signals, position sizing, and exit rules, yet the literature rarely identifies which component generates the return. We conduct a tick-level decomposition of a commercially deployed structural-break strategy on spot gold (XAUUSD, 2024–2026; 1,571 trades), isolating one component at a time under a controlled-variables design. Structural-break entry signals are the sole source of risk-adjusted alpha (annualized Sharpe ratio 2.6–3.1), robust to a random-entry placebo, multiple-testing correction, rolling windows, and slippage stress. Regime-conditional position sizing acts as implicit leverage and does not outperform constant-risk sizing. The asymmetric partial-exit raises the win rate but institutionalizes the disposition effect without adding risk-adjusted return. We also identify a methodological contingency: tick-data granularity may reshape component-level attribution in backtests. Confirming this preliminary finding will require full-coverage real-tick replication, which we leave to future work. The results discipline what counts as alpha in technical-trading research: most popular overlays reshape the return distribution without earning it.

title: The Constitutional Requirements for Legislators: Upholding Senatorial Qualifications under the Philippine Omnibus Election Code

detail.title: The Constitutional Requirements for Legislators: Upholding Senatorial Qualifications under the Philippine Omnibus Election Code
detail.abstract: This paper examines the constitutional discourse surrounding senatorial eligibility criteria in the Philippines under the 1987 Constitution and the Omnibus Election Code. In response to contemporary demands for electoral reform that propose more stringent academic or professional requirements to elevate legislative quality, this study argues for the preservation of existing baseline qualifications to protect democratic inclusivity and egalitarian franchise. Employing a constitutional and structural analysis, the study refutes the direct correlation between academic credentials and effective governance, demonstrating that altering these criteria risks worsening socioeconomic marginalization and fostering an elitist political landscape. Furthermore, using the principle of expressio unius est exclusio alterius, the paper highlights that modifying qualifications would necessitate complex, non-imperative charter changes while failing to dismantle entrenched structures like political dynasties. The study concludes that the true locus of power must remain with the sovereign electorate. Rather than imposing restrictive barriers, electoral integrity and merit-based choices should be achieved by empowering voters through multi-platform "Vote Wisely" campaigns, grassroots voter literacy seminars led by local government units, and absolute transparency regarding candidates' institutional track records.

title: Acting in Concert and Notification of Major Holdings: the CJEU Requires, in Principle, an 'Agreement' and Closes off National Extensions
affiliations: Sorbonne Law School

detail.title: Acting in Concert and Notification of Major Holdings: the CJEU Requires, in Principle, an 'Agreement' and Closes off National Extensions
detail.abstract: In its Valora judgment of 12 February 2026, delivered on a preliminary reference from the German Bundesgerichtshof, the Court of Justice of the European Union clarified the meaning of "acting in concert" in the law of major-holding notifications. The Court held that Article 3(1a) of the Transparency Directive (2004/109/EC, as amended by Directive 2013/50/EU) precludes national legislation extending notification obligations to holders of voting rights who have merely coordinated their conduct towards the issuer "in another way," absent an "agreement" within the meaning of Article 10(a), where that extension has no direct connection with takeover bids or other transactions affecting control. This comment argues that Valora effects a twofold tightening of the regime. First, on the scope of the concept: building on Adler (2021), the Court confirms the normative autonomy of concerted action in transparency law and reads the takeover-related derogation strictly, requiring a direct and specific link with rules belonging to takeover law and neutralising any extension based on similarity of purpose, possible application in an offer context, or insertion within a broader normative framework. Second, on its substance: the Court reaffirms the agreement as the necessary foundation of concerted action-coordination of conduct may serve only as evidence of a meeting of minds, never as an autonomous basis for characterisation. The paper assesses the consequences for French law, where Article L. 233-10 of the Commercial Code departs from Article 10(a) both in the object of the agreement (a "common policy in respect of the company" rather than a "lasting common policy towards the management of the issuer") and in its reach (extending to the acquisition or disposal of securities). It examines the tension between consistent interpretation and the structural divergence of the French definition, the questions referred by the Paris Court of Appeal (judgment of 18 December 2025), and concludes that legislative intervention-rather than continued judicial correction-is required to restore the intelligibility of positive law.

title: The Structure of Intellectual Property Law. Delimitations and Interferences between the Action for Trade Mark Infringement and the Action for Unfair Competition
affiliations: Florea Gheorghe and Associates SCPA

detail.title: The Structure of Intellectual Property Law. Delimitations and Interferences between the Action for Trade Mark Infringement and the Action for Unfair Competition

publicationDetails.detailsText: Published in the volume of the Annual Scientific Session ”Silence, Passivity and Inaction in the Architecture of the Law” of the ”Acad. Andrei Rădulescu” Institute of Legal Research of the Romanian Academy , 22 May 2026

detail.abstract: This paper examines the boundaries and overlaps between the legal regime applicable to infringement proceedings, a means of protecting exclusive trade mark rights over distinctive signs protected under the provisions of the Romanian Law No. 84/1998, and the legal regime governing actions for unfair competition, regulated in Romania under the Law No. 11/1991, a means of protecting competition and unregistered distinctive signs. Both actions seek to prohibit unlawful activities and are essential instruments for establishing competitive relationships on the market. Both actions aim to protect consumers against the risk of confusion between distinctive signs used by competing undertakings, as well as the undertakings themselves, against dilution, parasitism and denigration of signs used in commercial activities. One of the issues addressed in the paper concerns the interference between the two actions in terms of civil procedural law, in relation to the difficulty of qualification of unlawful acts, a matter of substantive law which falls within the jurisdiction of the courts and which requires the examination of evidence. The paper argues that, in accordance with the provisions of Article 22(4) of the Romanian Code of Civil Procedure, it is for the courts to qualify the civil action seeking to prohibit the use of a particular distinctive sign by a third party as an action for infringement of an exclusive trade mark right in an registered sign or an action for unfair competition, following an examination of the facts on which the specific claim brought before the court is based.

title: Fractured Families: The Unintended Consequences of Immigration Enforcement for Families
affiliations: George Mason University, George Mason University - Mercatus Center and George Mason University - Mercatus Center

detail.title: Fractured Families: The Unintended Consequences of Immigration Enforcement for Families
detail.abstract: Family integrity is an emergent result of individuals' attempts to coordinate plans on residence, caregiving, and economic support over time. U.S. immigration enforcement policies produce both intended and unintended consequences for the family, often undermining the stability of family units that are essential to society. Policies that separate children from parents at the border or detain and deport individual family members illustrate the direct use of the state to intentionally separate families. However, there are also unintended consequences of immigration policy that are of equal significance. Restrictions on circular migration have transformed temporary labor migration into long-term, often undocumented, settlement, forcing migrants to choose between financial support and physical presence with their family. Heightened border security has increased the danger of crossings, leading to ambiguous loss when migrants disappear in the desert, leaving family members in prolonged states of grief and uncertainty, disrupting short-and long-term plans. This paper argues that the consequences of U.S. immigration policy, whether intended or unintended, extend beyond the individual family unit and into the broader fabric of societies both domestically and internationally.
